item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Osana Akasuki,

As per the Required Reading, the last four sections of the template (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention Grabber, Additional Notes) should not exceed 400 words. Your post currently goes nearly 500 words over the limit. Please trim your post accordingly. For convenience, authors can use https://www.wordcounter.net to gauge their word count.

Once you've made the changes, please refer to this thread to contact reviewers: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

As an aside, I have no clue what you're attempting to pitch. If you're trying to create a meta article, you just… pitch it as normal. Having your writing be influenced by the anomaly is just hindering your ability to convey it properly, and prevents critters from properly providing feedback. Please edit your idea to present it in a more coherent manner.

And in case it isn't clear, roleplay is not allowed on the forums.

item.title: WIP SCP Idea (The Grand Conspiracy)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No, I want to see if people think it will work as an SCP and then develop it a bit more first

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, History??

Elevator Pitch: A viral Youtube video connecting a lot of the popular theories, things ranging from the Paul is dead theory, The Denver Airport, to the Black Knight Satellite, except this time the Foundation is thrown in and said to be the reason this all happened. The video has no anomalous properties, but it poses a threat to the secrecy of the Foundation.

Central Narrative: The idea isn’t fully fleshed out yet, but what I am aiming for is it to tell a story about the Foundation that connects about four to five popular conspiracy theories, with neutralized SCP reports, breach reports, operation reports, and all of those mixed in. The theory will likely be super far-fetched, and the reports featured in the video are speculated to be fakes, which leads to the comedy at the end - When in the form of an addendum, one of the personnel hints at some, if not all of the theory being true.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I think mainly the hook would be how the Foundation is connected to all of the theories, it’s going to be difficult but I want to write a lot of real-life events into it and explain it as an effect due to the Foundation.

Additional Notes: The reason why this isn’t something like an incident report is that the video was never taken down, due to the fact that it went viral within twenty-four hours and the Foundation doesn’t have a way to track and supply amnestics to all the people who watched it. They conducted an operation that tries to influence the video to be viewed as a joke instead. Also, this may confuse some of you, so I’ll make it a bit clearer, but all the theories will be a chain of events, not a collection of events handled by the Foundation separately.

item.title: Hmm... Is this related to a Forgotten Trope of Europe?
item.content:encoded:
Or Strange Minds Think Alike… Cool either way, but historical backing makes it cooler.

https://tvtropes.org/Main/ForgottenTrope

Older Than Steam:

Excessive mourning wakes the dead: The belief that excessive mourning disturbs the dead's rest was a fairly common superstition in Europe from the Middle Ages to about the eighteenth century. That's why English has the term 'wake' in the first place.

  • “The Unquiet Grave” is an English ballad sung from the perspective of a person note who mourns their dead lover for A Year and a Day. The lover then comes back as a ghost to haunt them, and begs the singer to stop mourning so they can have peace in the afterlife.
  • The Shroud is one of the fairy tales collected by The Brothers Grimm. The story is about a woman who weeps over her dead son day and night. One night, the boy's ghost asks her to stop mourning so he can rest in death.

item.content:encoded:
The blending of 'ink blob that commits mass murder' and 'ink blob that inserts itself into text' feels….weird here? Like the two things feel kinda…jarringly shoved together in a way that doesn't really blend together well for me. To be honest: both the mass murder and the text insertion are kinda…cliche at this point and I'm really not sure building on either will work unless you do something interesting with it, which brings me to my next thought.

There's not a lot of narrative meat to this; particularly since a lot of it seems to just be 'the scp keeps trying to escape' and like…that's a fine starting place for a story but the story has to end up going somewhere so this doesn't feel flat: something should change in regards to the escaping, whether it's the foundation figuring out a way to stop it, or the scp giving up, or the scp like, succeeding and escaping and doing something that means they can return to containment without the urge to escape again or something, y'know?

item.title: Re: The Lost Generation
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Article proceeds normally with several recovery logs detailing the circumstances surrounding particular subjects, most of which were only discovered after perpetrating acts of violence or suicide.

When you say 'subjects' here, do you mean 'the SCP' or 'people affected by the SCP'?

My broader concerns with this are two fold. Firstly, it kinda feels like this is really blurring the lines between 'real' and 'not real' to a point where I don't really have a clear idea of how this works. Specifically, you mention people have a like 'uncanny valley' reaction to them that leads them to be ostracised; but you also have this thing where folk who meet them can end up assuming they've been friends for a long time and it kinda feels like there's this awkward mesh where they both can and can't infiltrate society?

Thematically, a lot of this reminds me of SCP-4857 except it feels a lot blunter in it's questions.

My other big concern is that I'm not actually sure what this article will look like: the hook section indicates that there's meant to be this whole thing about being unsure if there's like, innocent people who have been arrested for crimes (and…I'm really not sure how that works: the implication of the infohazard is it only adds fake memories surrounding the SCP, not fake memories in general, and in turn, how can someone falsely remember murdering someone if they're still alive cos that implies they aren't an instance of the SCP?); but the additional notes imply this is meant to be much more about the effects of isolation in themes and I'm not sure how you're intending blending the two together.

item.title: Twisting Termite Tunnels
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not yet, I suppose…?

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-Fi, Nature Documentary, Comedy(?)

Elevator Pitch: Termites with a nest-building behavior that can bypass conventional spatial limitations, including covering immense distances and moving in and out of perfectly sealed spaces. Pretty much the same goals, needs, and individual intelligence of ordinary termites in all other respects.

Central Narrative: The first clue is the identification of Australian compass termites somewhere that they definitely should not be. Further investigation leads to exploration of their tunnels and the discovery that distant places are connected through seemingly-random twists and turns, which the insects have no trouble navigating but are confusing to a human sense of direction. There's a conspicuous lack of pocket dimensions, thaumaturgical Ways, or significant gravitational anomalies involved, at least as far as the Foundation can initially detect.

The Foundation would be up against mundane technological limitations on what sort of equipment can fit down an individual termite tunnel, as any substantial damage to the structures promptly collapses their anomalous effects.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We have an otherwise mostly mundane (if highly industrious) social insect species that cannot be reliably confined to a single habitat, although it's not an immediate Veil risk unless people start trying to identify individual termite species. What's more, they've created a functional hyperspace network out of nothing but soil and their own feces - and wouldn't the Foundation just love to learn how that works?

Additional Notes: Researching mundane eusocial insects is still relatively cutting-edge science, since they tend to live underground and it's hard to study large-scale emergent behaviors outside their natural habitat. I intend to research more into the kinds of technology used for these purposes, and play with how the Foundation might take them further. I could see this having a lot of experiment logs - perhaps taking reader suggestions, if the article were to take off.

item.title: SCP-XXXX Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Folklore/Drama/a slight bit of humor.

Page Layout: Standard Description and Containment Procedures, interview, incident report, and requests. The SCP and its procedures are currently under review by the foundation ethics committee.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a essentially a young man that grows a protective "carapace" of volcanic obsidian over any injury it receives. If the injury is enough to incapacitate or "kill" the subject it will instead become fully covered in this obsidian-like substance[in the visage of a wendigo from Algonquin folklore] and attempt to flee from or consume any living organism in its path. It must be noted that this material is impenetrable to known conventional means.

+ Central Narrative, Hook and Additional Notes
- collapse

Central Narrative: XXXX was discovered wandering along the highway after it was hit and incapacitated in a car crash on the I-15. Police reports indicate it terminated both the driver and all but one family member in the car before fleeing. Early interviews in containment suggest the entity gained its anomalous properties after being forced into a sanitarium for divergent behavior around the age of 14. This asylum in itself was an anomaly, unsanctioned and immoral "treatments" taking place on XXXX that would leave it with its anomalous properties. Basically, imagine "The Factory" but instead of churning out anomalous objects its anomalous humanoid entities.

XXXX eventually escapes and through various means carves out a living until its eventual containment at 18. While in containment the head researcher assigned for XXXX, Dr. Pharrow, petitions for the entity to be reclassified, hence the heavy involvement of the ethics committee throughout the article. Dr. Pharrow also fosters a sort of….friendship with the young man and begins to question the morality behind what the foundation does.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A unique entity that shifts the way a seasoned researcher sees anomalous humanoid SCPs. Perhaps it isn't all as black and white as he convinced himself it was.

Additional Notes: I…plan to pursue this sanitarium idea further in SCP Tales. I've most likely explained this poorly, and I apologize if so. Please do not hesitate to reply with questions or queries for clarification. Also if there is a similar SCP somewhere, please tell me, there are thousands of entries and I, nothing more than an inconsequential blip in the time span of this cosmos, am incapable of trawling through every one.

I wouldn't be surprised if even gods cannot alter such laws.

Through the tonal issues and various other problems I can't quite nail down in words myself, I can see a story here that I like. A desire to return to simpler times, put into practice with unforeseen consequences. An anomaly which was, in a sense, its own first victim, and is gradually becoming aware of this. An artist constrained by the rules of their own creation even as they start to see the flaws - but they're committed now, they can't unmake what was made. A living story written in permanent ink, mistakes and all.

I really wouldn't want to see this concept pass quietly into deletion just because it doesn't "feel like" the modern Foundation. I really hope some more experienced critics than me decide to weigh in on this.

Read: In most forums, you are actively discouraged from contacting mods except in major emergencies, while here it's par for the course.

I think there's a misunderstanding here—not all reviewers are moderators, and not all moderators are reviewers.

Since one of the main complaints we noted from reviewers was that authors would often ignore feedback unless they asked for it specifically, there was an attempt to shift focus towards authors reaching out to reviewers first to both familiarize themselves with how to ask/whom to ask, as well as confirming that there was an interest in continuing with the idea, rather than making the thread and then never responding to it.

It's true that you shouldn't need to message mods specifically, but reviewers can always be contacted when you're seeking a review.

item.title: Mr. Ink
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): -

Page Layout (Optional): -

Elevator Pitch: Mx. Ink (or Mr. Ink, any is fine) is a humanoid entity created as part of the Little Misters line. Their appearance varies, but is often reminiscent of a mime (minus the makeup, just the white face.) They're made up of a dense, tar-like substance and posses no real organs or anything similar to human anatomy. This would be the ink they're named after.

Due to their sadistic, cunning nature, Mr. Ink are contained in an air-tight metal barrel, thus preventing them from just going out and torturing any unsuspecting researcher. Since the liquid is so dense, Mr. Ink can make it seem like there's more of it than there actually is by making it less dense at will. They can't control the liquid unless it's all in one glob, if that makes any sense.

Apart from being able to control their body as a liquid, Mr. Ink can insert themselves into any text they come in contact with, though the text has to be written in black ink. (This part can be removed, since I know of other SCPs that do the text-changing trick)

Central Narrative: A little mister that will make all your stories more interesting! Careful, though, they're a bit snappy.

Mr. Ink was contained after a string of mysterious and twisted murders in a quiet neighborhood somewhere in London. They continually attempt to breach containment, and frequently resort to torturing researchers and interviewers they have access to.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As the SCP can manipulate texts to include them, it's up for debate if they're actually part of the Little Misters line, or just stole a Little Misters tag and added themselves to it for some reason.

Additional Notes: -

I have more ideas for this, so please feel free to ask questions if you want! This is my second SCP idea, so I'm still pretty inexperienced. I don't 100% get the new format either, so there's probably some info I've left out.

item.title: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Well, it was sort of meant for the group in general to see if I needed anything else.

Wikidot doesn't have a notifications system, so it's always best to send a PM when you're seeking further responses on a thread. Also, reviewers can't read minds, so it's always good to be straightforwardly clear when you're asking a question of everyone in the thread—in this case, the comment you posted seems like it was meant to be directed to an individual critiquer.

No offense, but this is one of the weirder forums out there, and the rules aren't that easy to figure out….

The forum guidelines are the way they are because in the past, very few reviewers were willing to assist authors because of the disconnect in communication and the lack of acknowledgement/conscientiousness of all the free favors reviewers are essentially doing. Please be mindful of the reviewers' perspective; they are often responding to multiple threads at once and aren't giving any one author special attention, and again, wikidot doesn't send them notifications letting them know when a thread is updated. Help them help you.

If the forum setup is difficult for you to follow, you can try seeking feedback in the IRC chatrooms, which offer real-time critique.

item.title: Re: SCP concept Investigator Carter
item.content:encoded:
I do not see how he is OP he is only immune to SCPs he creates. most of which are entirely harmless. He could get a bullet to the head and drop dead. Most of his anomalies dissipate within 24 hours because they are unstable.

He's still able to create anomalies that won't ever hurt him. Superficial weaknesses tacked on don't change that fact. You've also still got a whole pile of omniscient OP elements, like "He, also, seems to know of SCPs and how to find them and can create them." and "has been spotted at multiple sites of SCPs (31 known instances). He is drawn to SCPs for some anomalous reason".

It doesn't matter that the guy would presumably die like a normal human; the sheer amount of knowledge and elusiveness attributed to the guy already makes him pretty far removed from the average (normal, non-powered human) reader. Add on all the seemingly random abilities he has for no in-universe contextual reason, and it's pretty difficult for anyone to relate to the guy, let alone care about him enough to read his story.

If you really want to make this work, you're going to need to either scale down the abilities a lot, or develop your worldbuilding in a way that makes readers accept that it makes sense for the entity to have these abilities. So far what we're seeing in terms of character traits, abilities, and motives seems to be explained by "I want my character to be cool and always ahead of the Foundation", without any in-universe basis. Why does the guy investigate anomalies in the first place, and how will the audience find that interesting? Why does he seem to share knowledge of and the same focus as the Foundation, despite not being associated with the organization? And so on. Characters like these are often very difficult to write convincingly, so if you're intent on writing this as your first article, be prepared to put a lot of extra time and energy into revisions and reworks.
